why: Lina Malina's residence is a terraced Dogtown mansion above a container-zone street: a wide shuttered drive, an upper terrace with her chair and computer, and a roof hatch. Vanilla only staffs it for Dazed and Confused, when her Scavenger acting crew waits outside and she comes home at dark. This proposal loads the mansion's quest-design prefab, restores the five-person crew and their parked Archer Hella in their calm start/change poses, and leaves Lina herself to an owner decision because vanilla only stages her through the job's scene.

open_questions: Approach the residence from the street and confirm the five scavengers are outside, calm, in loitering poses and do not attack on sight.
Confirm all five are present and none is stuck in the phase-'change' pose used by scavenger_5 and scavenger_6 (sitting or smoking on the ledge).
Walk in through the front door under the runtime door policy; if it stays dead, note whether the window (Technical 20 / quickhack) or the roof hatch still gives a way in.
Check the upper flat reads as a home: sofa, Lina's chair, computer and terrace intact, with no shoot set, body or police tape.
Check the wide shutter and the roof hatch keep sensible states and do not seal the drive or the flat.
Check the parked Archer Hella sits in the drive and does not block the entrance.
Confirm no schedule display or other quest prop is visible on Lina's computer (var_schedule 0).

variant_toggles.why: Keeps the job's schedule display out of the flat. Vanilla shows it (var_schedule 1) while the mansion phase runs so V can break in and hack Lina's schedule to add the BD shoot; with no job there is no appointment to read. 0 is the other known state and the baked default; the runtime door/device state is otherwise vanilla.

proximity_wait.why: The flat's single entrance door (DoorControllerPS) in #loc_mq303_linas_mansion_devices: the normal way in for a visitor, so it is the first device a player reaches. The window and roof hatch are the job's break-in routes, not the way in.
